items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: you know those ragtime records you made with Charlie Love?

ctx.x: Did you both play the song there?

No, but I'll switch it off now. Uh, you know those ragtime records you made with Charlie Love? Yeah. Was that the part you were playing on the violin there, was that the same sort of stuff as you play with the superior? Yeah. The same lead.

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: I went up there with Frankie Duesen and Peter. Joe Oliver on the cornet. Joe Oliver. They had a dance at my home at the Artfellas. I went up there and wake all day with them fellas for nothing. I wasn't getting paid. I just wanted to play with them.

ctx.x: Right across the street is the little double house back in the yard. That's where Eddie used to live. Eddie Vinson and Tom Alvin on one side. Oh I see. And I used to go down there and join them every day. They had the bass violin player they called Teep. And when I first come down there I could play the bass. I was a little bit of a fellow. But Tom wanted the cornet playing. He said, get your cornet. We'll all show you. And Eddie Vinson played a vowel trombone you know. And he drilled me through what we were…

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: And Peter was in one of them society too, Peter Burkhardt. I wanted to be right with the gang, you know, so I said I might as well get in one too.

ctx.x: I wanted you to tell us about that joining up with the young men, what that was like.

Well that was a society, you know. You pay so much, let me see, was it every week? Every quarter, they'd have a meeting just like the union. I don't know, I believe it was a dollar a quarter or something like that. I can't remember exactly, but anyhow, when you die they bury you, you see. They give you a funeral and your wife or who you may be made out to, your sister or something, she get so much money. But it wasn't very much a couple of hundred or something like that. But they bury you know. The time I got…
Well, what's the difference between a society and a pleasure club?
